problem: Prior active inference work only runs in simulation with small, hand-designed state and sensor spaces, so it does not scale to high-dimensional real-world sensing such as camera frames.
motivation: Active inference is an influential theory of how biological agents perceive and act, but it has not been shown on real robots. Deep generative models can learn the state space end-to-end from raw pixels, which would remove the need to design states by hand.
key_idea: Implement the active inference generative model (posterior, prior, likelihood) as deep networks trained VAE-style on real camera and action data, then plan by choosing the policy with the lowest expected free energy computed on imagined rollouts.
insight: Learning the belief space from pixels lets active inference run on a real robot without a predefined state space. Preferences are specified by demonstration, using the state distribution seen while driving in the aisle middle, and this is enough to yield aisle-centering behaviour and recovery from pushes. There are no ablations or quantitative evaluations, so the evidence is only qualitative.
method: Generative model: a VAE-like sequential model with a convolutional encoder as posterior q_phi(s_t|s_{t-1},a_{t-1},o_t), a convolutional decoder as likelihood p_xi(o_t|s_t), and an LSTM as transition prior p_theta(s_t|s_{t-1},a_{t-1}); each outputs a diagonal Gaussian over a 128-d state.

Training objective: minimise variational free energy per timestep, i.e. the NLL of the observation plus KL(q_phi || p_theta), trained end-to-end for 1M iterations with Adam (lr 1e-4, batch 128, sequence length 10).
Data: 2 hours of Kuka Youbot driving in warehouse aisles, RGB from a RealSense camera (depth ignored), x/y/angular velocity actions at 10Hz, subsampled to 200ms steps.

Planning: three base policies (straight, left, right) are rolled out in imagination with p_theta and p_xi at horizons 10, 25 and 55, following Catal et al. 2020, and the expected free energy G is computed for each.
Action selection: the policy with lowest G is chosen (softmax with precision gamma=100), its first action is executed, and planning is repeated (receding horizon).
Preferences: the prior over preferred states is taken from the state distribution of demonstrations driving in the aisle middle.

setting.backbone: Conv encoder/decoder + LSTM deep generative model (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 2 hours of real-robot warehouse-aisle driving (RGB + velocity actions, 200ms subsampling)
setting.observation: monocular RGB camera frames (RealSense; depth unused)
setting.action_space: continuous x, y, angular velocities, selected from 3 base policies (straight, left, right)

numbers_note: No quantitative results; only qualitative figures and a video demo.
results: The robot navigates to and keeps driving in the middle of the aisle from random start poses, turns around at the aisle end, and recovers after being pushed. No metrics or baselines are reported.
limitations: Only qualitative demonstration on a simple aisle-following task; no quantitative metrics or baselines.
Preferred-state distributions and the set of policies to evaluate are hand-specified, and it is unclear how to define them for complex tasks.
The model cannot yet learn continuously from its own autonomous behaviour to fill gaps in the generative model.
builds_on: Catal et al. 2020 (learning perception and planning with deep active inference)
